passage: Note, Thursday. Nikita came to see me during the free period, straight-backed and a little pale. In the class group chat two friends had asked her to send a private photo taken at the sleepover "for the album". Nikita told them, "I'm not comfortable with that, please don't ask again." One friend said fine, and the other kept sending sad faces and "come on, don't be boring". Nikita said she felt guilty for hurting someone but still did not want to share it. I told her that saying no was her right and that a real friend accepts it. I asked her to keep the messages, and I spoke to the year coordinator with her permission. Gautam, class teacher.

qa.q: When did Nikita come to see her teacher?
qa.a: She came on Thursday, during the free period.

qa.q: What was Nikita feeling after she refused the photo request?
qa.a: She felt guilty about hurting one friend, yet she still wanted to keep her decision. Her pale face and straight back suggest she was also nervous.

qa.q: What could Nikita do if the second friend keeps pressing her?
qa.a: She could keep the messages, keep saying no, and tell a trusted adult again, as she already did.

qa.q: How might the friend who accepted the refusal see Nikita?
qa.a: That friend might respect Nikita more, seeing that Nikita can say no and still stay friendly.

grounding: A teenager sets a limit with a photo request, and an adult confirms refusal as a right and pressure as a warning sign.

passage:
Friday, late. Gautam's diary.

Today on the school trip Nikita said she wanted to post the picture of me asleep on the bus, the one with my mouth open. I said, "I'd rather not have that one posted." She laughed and said everyone would love it. My ears got hot. I said it again, slower: "I'm not okay with it. Please delete it."

She went quiet, then said, "Okay, sorry. I didn't think." She deleted it while I watched, and she even bought me a samosa at the rest stop.

I was scared she'd stop being my friend. She didn't. I told Papa tonight anyway, because I want him to know I said no and it worked.

qa.q: What was the picture Nikita wanted to post?
qa.a: It was the picture of Gautam asleep on the bus with an open mouth.

qa.q: Why did Gautam say it again, more slowly, the second time?
qa.a: Gautam probably felt nervous and wanted to make sure she understood the no was meant, since Gautam's ears got hot. Gautam might also have feared she would laugh it off again.

qa.q: What did Gautam do well when Nikita laughed?
qa.a: Gautam stayed calm, said no again clearly and asked for the picture to be deleted, so her joking could not turn the refusal into a joke. 🙂

qa.q: How might Nikita have felt when Gautam said it again?
qa.a: She may have felt embarrassed at first, then realised she had not thought about Gautam's feelings, and the samosa suggests she wanted to make up for it.

grounding: A teenager sets a limit about a photo in a diary, and a friend respects it.

passage:
After the evening prayer at the village temple, Shalini pulled Sarika behind the flower stall.
"My cousin from Nashik wants your number. He saw you at the fair. Just give it, na? And don't tell your Amma, she'll make a big thing."
Sarika's fingers tightened on her dupatta. "I'm not comfortable giving my number to someone I don't know."
"Don't be so boring. He's nice. I promised him."
"Then that's your promise. Not mine. No."
Shalini rolled her eyes and walked off in a huff.
Walking home along the canal, Sarika kept thinking about "don't tell your Amma." That was the part that felt wrong.
At dinner she told Amma everything. Amma listened, put a hand on her head and said, "You did right. Both times." That same night she went next door and spoke to Shalini's mother, calmly, about the cousin.

qa.q: Where did Shalini pull Sarika after the evening prayer?
qa.a: She pulled Sarika behind the flower stall at the village temple.

qa.q: What was Sarika feeling as she walked home along the canal?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and troubled, because Shalini's "don't tell your Amma" felt wrong even after she had refused.

qa.q: How did Amma support Sarika well?
qa.a: Amma listened, praised Sarika for saying no and for telling, and spoke to Shalini's mother that same night instead of waiting.

qa.q: How might Shalini see the refusal compared with Sarika?
qa.a: Shalini seems to see it as Sarika being boring and making her break a promise, while Sarika sees a stranger asking for her number in secret.

grounding: The scene shows a teenager refusing to share her number, recognising secrecy and pressure as warning signs, and telling a trusted adult who acts.

passage:
It was Friday evening in Bergen, and the rain had finally stopped. Freya knocked on Santiago's door with her skateboard under her arm.
"Skatepark, now! Everyone's there."
Santiago was in his socks, a half-built model boat on the table. He had been at school, then football, then helping his grandmother with shopping.
"I'm not up for it tonight," he said. "I need a quiet evening."
Freya lowered the board. "Really? You love Fridays."
"I do. Just not this one."
For a second she looked disappointed. Then she shrugged and smiled. "Okay. Save me a slice of whatever your grandmother made?"
"Deal."
She rolled off down the wet street. Santiago shut the door and noticed his shoulders drop. On Sunday Freya texted, "Rested? Park?" and he said yes straight away.

qa.q: What was on Santiago's table when Freya knocked?
qa.a: A half-built model boat was on the table.

qa.q: What was Santiago feeling when he said he wasn't up for it?
qa.a: He was tired after a full day and wanted calm, and his shoulders dropping after the door shut suggests he felt relieved his no was accepted.

qa.q: What made this a good way to set a limit?
qa.a: Santiago said clearly what he needed without making excuses or blaming Freya, so it was easy for her to accept.

qa.q: How did Freya show she was a true friend?
qa.a: She felt a moment of disappointment but respected his no without pushing, and asked again on Sunday, which made him happy to say yes.

grounding: The scene shows a teenager setting a limit with a friend and the friend respecting it.

passage: The robotics club room at the community centre smelled of solder and samosas. Sunaina had just taken a group photo beside their line-following robot and was already typing a caption for the club page. "Wait," Eshaan said. His cheek was still puffed up from the dentist that morning, and in the photo he looked like he was hiding a golf ball in it. He kept his voice even. "I'm not okay with that one going up. Can you crop me out or take another?" Karan groaned. "Bro, it's funny. Nobody cares." Eshaan's ears went hot, but he didn't laugh along. "I care. It's my face." Sunaina looked from one to the other, then deleted the photo right there and turned the screen so Eshaan could see. "Retake, everyone. Eshaan, stand behind the flag." Karan muttered, but he posed. Afterwards Sunaina said quietly, "Thanks for just saying it. I'd rather know."

qa.q: Why was Eshaan's cheek puffed up?
qa.a: Eshaan's cheek was still puffed up from the dentist that morning.

qa.q: What was Eshaan feeling when Karan called the photo funny?
qa.a: Eshaan felt embarrassed and a bit pressured, his ears going hot, yet steady enough not to laugh along. He may also have been worried about the whole club seeing it.

qa.q: Which choice worked, and why?
qa.a: Eshaan named the limit calmly and offered options, crop or retake, and Sunaina deleted it on the spot, so the refusal was respected without a fight. 👍

qa.q: What was it like for Sunaina when Eshaan said no?
qa.a: Sunaina seemed grateful rather than annoyed, saying she'd rather know, so the limit made things between them easier, not harder.

grounding: It shows a teenager setting a calm limit about sharing a photo, one peer respecting it at once, and another's pressure being met with a steady no.
